title: Catalog availability lags reservations
summary: Browse clients continue to show available stock for items that recent reservations could not claim.
precursor: The catalog service was rolled out in stages while product availability updates continued at their usual rate.
impact: Customers encounter rejected reservations after selecting apparently available items, increasing checkout abandonment and support contacts.

title: Inventory snapshot updates fall behind write bursts
summary: Inventory reads intermittently disagree with completed reservations, most often during busy periods.
precursor: A nightly stock reconciliation overlapped with a promotion that sharply increased reservation writes.
impact: Fulfillment decisions use outdated quantities, requiring manual order review and delaying shipment allocation.

title: Session lookups degrade during profile fetches
summary: Sign-in and checkout requests intermittently pause or ask users to retry, while other account pages remain responsive.
precursor: The account profile service shifted traffic to a secondary region during a maintenance window.
impact: More authentication attempts expire at the client, increasing abandoned checkouts and repeated login requests.

title: Price changes arrive late in browse listings
summary: Administrators see updated prices before the same products show those prices in customer listings.
precursor: A bulk catalog import emitted a much larger-than-normal set of product change events ahead of a weekend sale.
impact: Customers receive inconsistent prices between browse and checkout flows, prompting manual adjustments and delaying order confirmation.

title: Browse latency climbs after cache settings rollout
summary: Product-list latency and backing-store traffic rise sharply after a routine rollout, although the service remains available.
precursor: A configuration bundle for the new listing deployment was promoted shortly before the morning traffic peak.
impact: Category pages load more slowly and database capacity headroom falls, increasing the risk of broader catalog degradation.
